facts: This is an appeal by certificate granted by the High Court under Article 133(1)(c) of the Constitution of India

A charge-sheet was served on him levelling certain charges of alleged misconduct. In pursuance of an inquiry the appellant was dismissed from the office of the Principal of school by a resolution dated February 8, 1967 passed by the Managing Committee of the School (respondent 1 herein).

The President of the Board of Secondary Education after hearing the parties allowed the appeal, set aside the order of dismissal, and issued certain consequential directions to respondent 1, Managing Committee.

The High Court quashed the order of the President of the Board of Secondary Education on the ground that no appeal to him was competent having regard to the fact that the dismissed Principal had not yet been confirmed.

It appears that this very question had come up before another bench of the very same High Court in Kailash Choudhary v. President of the Board of Secondary Education , wherein the view has been taken that inasmuch as the termination of the services of the Principal stemmed from a finding of guilt recorded against him in a departmental proceeding which casts a stigma he had a right of appeal as a teacher.
Whether or not the Principal was a confirmed Principal or not is irrelevant inasmuch as under the rules, an appeal is provided against an order of dismissal.
issues: whether a Principal of a School who has not yet been confirmed can prefer an appeal to the President of the Board of Secondary Education
petitioner_arguments: The decision in Kailash Choudhary case , reflects the correct position of law.
An appeal is therefore competent under the relevant rule as rightly held in Kailash Choudhary case .
The order passed by the High Court must be set aside.
court_reasoning: We are of the opinion that the decision in Kailash Choudhary case , reflects the correct position of law.
Whether or not the Principal was a confirmed Principal or not is irrelevant inasmuch as under the rules, an appeal is provided against an order of dismissal.
holding: The appeal must, therefore, be allowed.
The order passed by the High Court must be set aside.
The order dated August 28, 1968 passed by the President of Board of Secondary Education will stand restored and will be given effect to.
